research.topic: Table tennis originated in Victorian England in the 1880s as an after-dinner parlour game, improvised on dining tables with books as a net and cigar-box lids or champagne corks (Britannica; ITTF). The name 'Ping-Pong' was trademarked by J. Jaques & Son in London in 1901, when sets and rules were sold commercially; the ITTF was founded in 1926 and the first World Championships were held in London that December. Table tennis joined the Olympic programme at Seoul 1988; through Paris 2024 China has won 37 of the 42 gold medals; Japan 1 (mixed doubles, Tokyo 2020); Great Britain none.

myths.reality: China dominates it (37 of 42 Olympic golds) but the game began as a Victorian parlour pastime in England in the 1880s; commercial sets and rules appeared in London around 1901.
